---
title: "Copy Number Variation"
---


```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
devtools::load_all()
library(tidyverse)
library(kableExtra)
library(psych)
library(ecp)
```

The `ecp` package comes with a microarray dataset `ACGH` (`n=2215; p=43`). This is a Copy Number Variation (CNV) dataset. The x-axis corresponds to position on the genome, whereas the y-axis corresponds to the ratio of copy numbers between healthy and sick populations. Based on the theoretical understanding, we do not expect any correlation between individuals. There is no reason the variation in the copy number of one individual to correspond to another individuals. 

This is a good dataset to apply the diagonal tests on. From theoretical understanding, we expect the covariance matrix to be diagonal. 

```{R plot-acgh-microarray-data} 
#| echo: false

# Load Data
data("ACGH", package="ecp") # microarray data
X <- ACGH$data
n <- nrow(ACGH$data)
p <- ncol(ACGH$data)

# Plot Data (10 x 1)
par(mfrow = c(10, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:10) {
  plot(X[, i], type = "l", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
        ylab = colnames(X)[i], cex.lab = 0.8)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
}
axis(1)
mtext("Probe index", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

Notice that at the very end, there is this severe drop. This is because the probes correspond to sex chromosomes, making the copy number less reliable. We follow `Bleakley and Vert (2011)` and remove these for stability so our final data dimension is `n=2143, p=43`.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## ACF

```{R plot-acgh-acf}
#| echo: false

# Plot ACF (10 x 1)
par(mfrow = c(10, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:10) {
  res <- SIP::SIP.acf(X[, i], plot = FALSE)
  lag <- res$lag
  acf <- res$acf
  bar_col <- ifelse(abs(acf) > res$h0.ci, "red", "black")
  plot(lag, acf, type = "h", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n", ylab = "",
        ylim = c(-0.2, 0.5), col = bar_col)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
  abline(h = 0)
  abline(h = c(-1, 1) * res$h0.ci, col = "blue", lty = 2)
}
axis(1, at = lag)
mtext("Lag", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

## Trend

```{R plot-acgh-running-ece}
#| echo: false

S <- ece_terms(X[, 1:5])
k <- 25
S_smooth <- stats::filter(S, rep(1/k, k), sides = 2)
pair_idx <- combn(5, 2)

# Plot ECE terms (10 x 1)
par(mfrow = c(10, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:10) {
  ylim <- quantile(S[, i], probs = c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)
  pair_label <- paste(pair_idx[1, i], pair_idx[2, i], sep = "-")
  plot(S[, i], type = "l", col = "lightgray", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
        ylab = pair_label, cex.lab = 0.8, ylim = ylim)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
  abline(h = mean(S[, i]), col = "blue")
  lines(S_smooth[, i])
  legend("topright", legend = sprintf("%.3f", mean(S[, i])),
         text.col = "blue", bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
}
axis(1)
mtext("Probe index", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

:::

```{R table-acgh-pvalues}
#| echo: false
set.seed(123)
results <- data.frame(
  Method  = c(
    "Bootstrap Multiplier",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (PSD)",
    "Parametric Bootstrap",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (PSD, Centered)",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (PSD, Normalized)",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (PSD, Centered + Normalized)",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (Naive)",
    "Bartlett Test"
  ),
  `p-value` = c(
    round(test.diag(X, method="bs.multiplier")$p.value, 3),
    round(test.diag(X, method="bs.parametric.psd")$p.value, 3),
    NA,
    round(test.diag(X, method="bs.parametric.psd.center")$p.value, 3),
    round(test.diag(X, method="bs.parametric.psd.norm")$p.value, 3),
    round(bs_parametric_test(X, force_psd = TRUE, center = TRUE, normalize = TRUE)$p.value, 3),
    round(bs_parametric_naive_test(X)$p.value, 3),
    round(cortest.bartlett(cor(X), nrow(X))$p.value)
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)

kable(results, align = c("l", "c"), na = "—") |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

**Observations**:

- As expected, both parametric bootstrap and bootstrap multiplier fail to reject the null hypothesis
- Parametric bootstrap produces a non-PSD covariance matrix, so the PSD correction is necessary
- Classical methods that do not account for mean shifts strongly reject the null hypothesis
- Centering and normalization both move the parametric bootstrap p-value away from the rejection boundary (PSD: 0.053; centered: 0.081; normalized: 0.126; both: 0.141). The conclusion at $\alpha = 0.05$ does not change, but the plain PSD version is borderline

```{R cnv-cor-heatmap-helper}
#| echo: false

cnv_plot_cor_heatmap <- function(cor_mat, pval_mat, fill_lab) {
  cor_df <- as.data.frame(cor_mat) |>
    rownames_to_column("Series1") |>
    pivot_longer(-Series1, names_to = "Series2", values_to = "correlation")
  pval_df <- as.data.frame(pval_mat) |>
    rownames_to_column("Series1") |>
    pivot_longer(-Series1, names_to = "Series2", values_to = "p_value")
  df <- left_join(cor_df, pval_df, by = c("Series1", "Series2"))
  bound <- max(abs(df$correlation))
  sig_df <- df |> filter(Series1 != Series2, p_value < 0.05)

  ggplot(df, aes(x = Series1, y = Series2, fill = correlation)) +
    geom_tile() +
    geom_text(data = sig_df, aes(label = "*"), color = "black", size = 3, vjust = 0.75) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "steelblue", mid = "white", high = "firebrick", midpoint = 0, limits = c(-bound, bound)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 6), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = fill_lab)
}

# Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment on the unique off-diagonal p-values (each pair
# appears twice in a symmetric p-value matrix; adjusting the full vectorized
# matrix would double-count every test and treat the zeroed diagonal as p more
# tests).
cnv_bh_adjust_pmat <- function(pmat) {
  p   <- ncol(pmat)
  idx <- combn(p, 2)
  q   <- p.adjust(pmat[cbind(idx[1, ], idx[2, ])], method = "BH")
  qmat <- matrix(NA_real_, p, p, dimnames = dimnames(pmat))
  qmat[cbind(idx[1, ], idx[2, ])] <- q
  qmat[cbind(idx[2, ], idx[1, ])] <- q
  diag(qmat) <- 0
  qmat
}

# Null-restricted z-test (rho = 0): under the theoretical null that individuals'
# copy-number ratios are uncorrelated, only k22 needs estimating, since every
# other kappa term carries a factor of rho or rho^2 and drops out algebraically
# at rho = 0.
cnv_ece_pval_null <- function(X) {
  p <- ncol(X)
  pval_mat <- matrix(NA, p, p)
  colnames(pval_mat) <- rownames(pval_mat) <- colnames(X)
  for (i in 1:(p - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):p) {
      pair <- cbind(X[, i], X[, j])
      pval <- ece.test(pair, type = "z.test", kappa = ece.kappa(pair, rho = 0, method = "mom"), rho = 0)$p.value
      pval_mat[i, j] <- pval
      pval_mat[j, i] <- pval
    }
  }
  diag(pval_mat) <- 0
  pval_mat
}
```

### Results

```{R cnv-cor-histogram}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-cnv-cor-histogram
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of pairwise correlations, Pearson vs. ECE."

cnv_cor_mat <- cor(X, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
cnv_ece_cor <- ece.cor(X)
dimnames(cnv_ece_cor) <- dimnames(cnv_cor_mat)

pair_idx <- combn(ncol(X), 2)
cnv_cor_df <- data.frame(
  method = rep(c("Pearson", "ECE"), each = ncol(pair_idx)),
  correlation = c(cnv_cor_mat[t(pair_idx)], cnv_ece_cor[t(pair_idx)])
)
cnv_cor_means <- cnv_cor_df |> summarise(mean = mean(correlation), .by = method)

ggplot(cnv_cor_df, aes(x = correlation, fill = method)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), breaks = seq(-1, 1, by = 0.05),
                  position = "identity", alpha = 0.5, color = "white") +
  geom_vline(data = cnv_cor_means, aes(xintercept = mean, color = method),
              linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Pearson" = "firebrick", "ECE" = "steelblue")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Pearson" = "firebrick", "ECE" = "steelblue")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Estimated correlation", y = "Density", fill = NULL)
```

---

We can also single out the pairs with the largest-magnitude covariance and inspect them directly.

```{R identify-max-pair}
#| echo: false
S_cov <- ece.cov(X)
diag(S_cov) <- 0
pair_ij <- which(upper.tri(S_cov), arr.ind = TRUE)
top_pairs <- data.frame(i = pair_ij[, 1], j = pair_ij[, 2], val = S_cov[pair_ij])
top_pairs <- top_pairs[order(-abs(top_pairs$val)), ][1:3, ]
top_cols <- unique(c(top_pairs$i, top_pairs$j))
```

The three largest-magnitude pairs are series `r paste(top_pairs$i, top_pairs$j, sep = "-", collapse = ", ")`, with $\hat\Sigma$ = `r paste(round(top_pairs$val, 3), collapse = ", ")`, respectively.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Plot

```{R plot-max-pair}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(length(top_cols), 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (col in top_cols) {
  plot(X[, col], type = "l", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n", ylab = col, cex.lab = 0.8)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
}
axis(1)
mtext("Probe index", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

## Trend

```{R trend-max-pair}
#| echo: false

k <- 25
par(mfrow = c(3, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (r in 1:3) {
  i <- top_pairs$i[r]
  j <- top_pairs$j[r]
  S_term <- ece_terms(X[, c(i, j)])[, 1]
  S_term_smooth <- stats::filter(S_term, rep(1/k, k), sides = 2)
  ylim <- quantile(S_term, probs = c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)
  plot(S_term, type = "l", col = "lightgray", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
        ylab = paste(i, j, sep = "-"), cex.lab = 0.8, ylim = ylim)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
  abline(h = mean(S_term), col = "blue")
  lines(S_term_smooth)
  legend("topright", legend = sprintf("%.3f", mean(S_term)),
         text.col = "blue", bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
}
axis(1)
mtext("Probe index", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

## Remove Outlier

```{R table-acgh-pvalues-remove-outlier}
#| echo: false
X <- ACGH$data[1:2143,][-1992,]
set.seed(123)
results <- data.frame(
  Method  = c(
    "Bootstrap Multiplier",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (PSD)",
    "Parametric Bootstrap",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (PSD, Centered)",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (PSD, Normalized)",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (PSD, Centered + Normalized)",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (Naive)",
    "Bartlett Test"
  ),
  `p-value` = c(
    round(test.diag(X, method="bs.multiplier")$p.value, 3),
    round(test.diag(X, method="bs.parametric.psd")$p.value, 3),
    NA,
    round(test.diag(X, method="bs.parametric.psd.center")$p.value, 3),
    round(test.diag(X, method="bs.parametric.psd.norm")$p.value, 3),
    round(bs_parametric_test(X, force_psd = TRUE, center = TRUE, normalize = TRUE)$p.value, 3),
    round(bs_parametric_naive_test(X)$p.value, 3),
    round(cortest.bartlett(cor(X), nrow(X))$p.value)
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)

kable(results, align = c("l", "c"), na = "—") |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

axis(1)
mtext("Probe index", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
